decisive_items: Few, micro-ischemic focal lesions in the periventricular and deep white matter of the cerebral hemispheres
Mild cerebral atrophy/aging more pronounced in the curvatures of the cerebral hemispheres
response.rationale: MRI shows micro-ischemic white matter lesions and cerebral atrophy, hallmark features of cerebral small vessel disease; comorbid depression/anxiety and cognitive symptoms are consistent. R6 is broader but less specific, while other candidates lack direct imaging support or have contradicting features.

rejected.why: Depression and anxiety are comorbid symptoms, not supported as the primary diagnosis by imaging.
MMSE supports cognitive impairment, but micro-ischemic lesions indicate a vascular etiology rather than primary depression.
Only partially empty sella is present; no ventriculomegaly or clinical triad to support NPH.
Depression is comorbid and lacks independent diagnostic support.
No subdural collection or examination findings; atrophy is nonspecific.
Cognitive score improved after treatment and lacks progressive dementia features; micro-ischemic lesions alone are insufficient.
Anxiety is comorbid and not supported by imaging findings.
Atrophy is nonspecific and micro-ischemic lesions point to vascular rather than primary neurodegeneration.
Leg pain alone is insufficient; MRI findings and left-sided difficulties indicate central nervous system involvement.
